title.narrative: Seventh Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Program in Ecuador

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The GEF-7 project is designed under the idea of achieving social and environmental benefits through strengthening of bio-enterprise networks in areas of global biodiversity importance. The GEF-7 project will support planning and management of landscapes with globally significant biodiversity, using a multifocal, multi-sectoral approach, and overcoming organizational barriers to the use of land for sustainable production and connectivity. The project will increase the socio-economic benefits to stakeholders in the identified areas and other later-linked participants through sustainable use of biodiversity and other resources in these landscapes, using the improved methodology for “Products with Territorial Identity” developed by SGP during GEF-6. These initiatives will be supported in areas such as food security and land use and sustainability through a community-based natural resource management strategy, directly connected to the new development plan of Ecuador to procure income-generating activities while promoting biodiversity conservation. As an indirect result, these include improved soil productivity through agroecological practices and production systems, containing use of compost and organic fertilizer; improved micro-climate and water resource availability and volume from windbreaks, agroforestry systems, and cover crops; conservation and sustainable use of crop genetic biodiversity; greater pest control from agroecological, poly-cultural systems; as well as others to be identified and innovated by smallholder organizations. At the same time, with the landscape planning approach, ecosystem services are identified for enhancement, providing substantial benefits to communities beyond the program’s direct area of influence. The ecosystem services provided by the Paramo, which include water retention, regulation, and carbon sequestration, are retained by setting aside areas for conservation, as well as through improved soil, water, and biomass management in the production landscape. The conservation of dry forest ecosystems and associated coastal mangroves provide direct benefits to communities through improved availability of marine fauna and flora for sustainable harvesting. Conservation or regeneration of coastal habitats provide protection of shorelines from erosion, tsunamis, and storms. Generally, natural resources management and product development know-how can be very unequal between the private sector and communitarian entrepreneurships. Companies tend to keep this information as proprietary secrets even when communities are somehow involved in the process. This problem could be mitigated by clearly identifying rights and obligations of both parties and enforcing them to ensure knowledge transference.

To enable community networks to build social, economic and ecological resilience through bio-enterprises in nine landscapes located in the coastal, highlands and Amazon region for global environmental benefits and sustainable development
